add_review.description: Leave your account's review of an item, with an optional star rating. One account has one review per item, so running this again replaces what was there. The review is queued as a background task and appears on the item's page once that task runs.
add_review.name: add_review

parameters.description: The item to review.
parameters.name: identifier

parameters.description: The heading shown above the review.
parameters.name: title

parameters.description: What you want to say about the item.
parameters.name: body

parameters.description: A rating from 0 to 5. Leave blank to review the item without rating it.
parameters.name: stars

check_identifier.description: Check whether an identifier is free before creating an item with it. An identifier is an item's permanent name and the last part of its archive.org URL, and it cannot be changed casually afterwards. Also applies archive.org's own rules about what a name may be: 5 to 100 characters, letters, digits, periods, underscores and dashes, which the site's availability check does not.
check_identifier.display_str_template: Check whether the identifier {0} is free.

mock_response.message: The identifier you have chosen is available

check_identifier.name: check_identifier

parameters.description: The identifier you want to claim.
parameters.name: identifier

create_item.description: Create a new item on archive.org and put its first file in it. The identifier becomes the item's permanent name and the last part of its URL, so check it is free first. archive.org accepts the file straight away and ingests it in the background, so the item's page can take a few minutes to appear. Everything uploaded here is public. If the identifier is already taken the step stops rather than quietly dropping the metadata below - archive.org only reads it while an item is being made - unless you turn on 'Add to it if it already exists'.
create_item.name: create_item

parameters.description: The permanent name for the new item: 5 to 100 characters, letters, digits, periods, underscores and dashes. It must not already be taken.
parameters.name: identifier

parameters.description: The file to upload: choose a file, or point at a document produced by an earlier step.
parameters.name: file

parameters.description: The name to store the file under. Filled in from the file you choose; change it to store it under a different name.
parameters.name: file_name

parameters.description: What kind of thing this item is. This decides how archive.org displays it and which derivatives it generates, and it cannot be changed casually later. Defaults to Data. Collection and Etree are only accepted from accounts archive.org has granted them to.
parameters.name: media_type

options.label: Collection: an item that holds other items

parameters.description: Which open collection to file the item under. Use the test collection while you are trying this out: archive.org removes its items after 30 days. To use a collection you administer yourself, set 'collection' under Additional metadata instead. This only applies while the item is being made: moving an item between collections afterwards needs a privilege ordinary accounts do not have.
parameters.name: collection

options.label: Test collection: sandbox, removed after 30 days

parameters.description: The item's title, as it appears on its page.
parameters.name: title

parameters.description: What the item is. Basic HTML is allowed, and links in it are rendered.
parameters.name: description

parameters.description: Who made the thing being archived: the author, artist, photographer or organisation.
parameters.name: creator

parameters.description: When the thing being archived was made or published, not when it is being uploaded.
parameters.name: item_date

parameters.description: Subject tags for the item. These are what a subject search matches on.
parameters.name: subjects

parameters.description: Any other metadata fields to set, as field names and values: 'language', 'licenseurl', 'publisher', or a field of your own. Also how to file the item into a collection you administer.
parameters.name: custom_metadata

parameters.description: Whether archive.org should generate the thumbnails, transcodes and OCR text it makes from an upload. On by default; turn it off when several files are going into one item and only the last should trigger it.
parameters.name: queue_derive

parameters.description: By default this step stops if the identifier is already taken, because archive.org only reads the metadata above while an item is being made and would quietly keep the existing item's instead. Turn this on to upload the file into that item and apply these fields through the metadata API, which is what makes the step safe to re-run. Media type and collection are left alone on an item that already exists - changing either moves or re-types it, which archive.org only allows privileged accounts to do - and come back in 'metadata_skipped'.
parameters.display_name: Add to it if it already exists
parameters.name: allow_existing

delete_file.description: Remove one file from an item. The item itself stays, and so do its other files. Turn on 'Also delete derivatives' to take the thumbnails, OCR text and transcodes archive.org generated from this file with it.
delete_file.display_str_template: Delete {1} from the Internet Archive item {0}.
delete_file.name: delete_file

parameters.description: The item the file to delete belongs to.
parameters.name: identifier

parameters.description: The file to delete, chosen from the item's own file list.
parameters.name: file_name

parameters.description: Delete the files archive.org generated from this one as well. Without this they are left behind, pointing at an original that is gone.
parameters.name: cascade_delete

parameters.description: Move the file into the item's history rather than removing it outright.
parameters.display_name: Keep a copy in the item's history
parameters.name: keep_old_version

delete_review.description: Remove your account's review of an item. Deleting a review that was never written is not an error: it answers that there was nothing to remove.
delete_review.display_str_template: Delete your Internet Archive review of {0}.
delete_review.name: delete_review

parameters.description: The item to remove your review from.
parameters.name: identifier

download_file.description: Fetch one file out of an item and keep it as a document a later step can read, attach or send on. The bytes come straight from the data node holding the item. Files up to 200 MB; for anything larger, use the download URL 'List item files' returns.
download_file.display_str_template: Download {1} from the Internet Archive item {0}.
download_file.name: download_file

parameters.description: The item the file to download belongs to.
parameters.name: identifier

parameters.description: The file to download, chosen from the item's own file list. Nested names such as 'folder/page.jpg' are fine.
parameters.name: file_name

get_item.description: Everything archive.org knows about one item in a single request: its descriptive metadata, the files it holds with their sizes, formats, checksums and download URLs, its total size, when it was last changed, and whether it has been hidden. The embedded file list is capped at 100 entries: use 'List item files' to page through a larger one.
get_item.name: get_item

parameters.description: The item to read. Accepts an identifier or an archive.org URL.
parameters.name: identifier

get_item_field.description: Read one part of an item's record instead of all of it: its size, the date it last changed, its descriptive metadata, or one entry from its file list. Much smaller than 'Get an item' when the item holds thousands of files, and the only way to slice a long list with a start and a count.
get_item_field.name: get_item_field

parameters.description: The item to read a field from.
parameters.name: identifier

parameters.description: Which part of the item's record to read.
parameters.name: field_name

options.label: metadata: the item's own descriptive fields
files_count: how many files the item holds
item_size: the item's total size in bytes
created: when this metadata record was generated
item_last_updated: when the item last changed
server: the data node currently serving the item
d1: the item's primary data node
d2: the item's secondary data node
dir: the item's path on its data node
workable_servers: every node that can serve it
is_dark: whether the item has been hidden
uniq: the record's cache-busting revision number

parameters.description: Optional. Go one level deeper: a field name under 'metadata' (such as 'title'), or a zero-based position in a list (such as '0' for the first file).
parameters.name: subfield

parameters.description: Optional. For a field that is a list, the zero-based position to start from.
parameters.name: start

parameters.description: Optional. For a field that is a list, how many entries to return from the starting position.
parameters.name: count

get_item_view_details.description: Where an item's views came from: a breakdown by country and region with coordinates, split between human and robot traffic, plus the pages that linked to the item over the same window. Give a start and end date for a fixed period, or a number of days for a rolling one.
get_item_view_details.display_str_template: Get Internet Archive view details for {0}.
get_item_view_details.name: get_item_view_details

parameters.description: The item to break down.
parameters.name: identifier

parameters.description: The first day to count. Give this with an end date for a fixed period; leave both blank to use a rolling window instead. archive.org's view data starts on 1 January 2017.
parameters.name: start_date

parameters.description: The last day to count. Required if a start date is given.
parameters.name: end_date

parameters.description: Count the last N days instead of a fixed period. Ignored when a start and end date are given. Defaults to 30.
parameters.name: last_n_days

parameters.description: How many of the busiest places and referrers to return (1-1000). Defaults to 100.
parameters.name: max_rows

get_item_views.description: How often items have been viewed: all time, over the last 30 days, and over the last 7. Takes up to 50 identifiers at once, so a whole collection's headline numbers are one step.
get_item_views.display_str_template: Get Internet Archive view counts for {0}.
get_item_views.name: get_item_views

parameters.description: The items to count, up to 50. Point this at an earlier search step to report on everything it found.
parameters.name: identifiers

get_item_views_per_day.description: A day-by-day view series for items, split between human traffic, robots and requests archive.org could not classify. One row per date, newest last, ready to chart. archive.org holds this data from 1 January 2017 onward and publishes it with a few weeks' lag.
get_item_views_per_day.display_str_template: Get daily Internet Archive view counts for {0}.
get_item_views_per_day.name: get_item_views_per_day

parameters.description: The items to chart, up to 50.
parameters.name: identifiers

parameters.description: How many days back to return, ending at the most recent day archive.org has published. Defaults to 30.
parameters.name: days

get_review.description: Read the review your account has left on an item, with its title, body, star rating and the dates it was written and last changed. archive.org's reviews API is scoped to the connected account, so this reads your own review rather than the item's whole review list. Not having written one is not an error: it answers 'has_review: false'.
get_review.display_str_template: Get your Internet Archive review of {0}.

review.reviewbody: Decades of imagery, all freely available.

get_review.name: get_review

parameters.description: The item to read your review of.
parameters.name: identifier

get_task_log.description: Read what a task actually did. This is where a failed upload, derive or metadata change says why. Logs run to megabytes on large items, so this returns the last lines, which is where a failure states itself, and reports how many there were in total. A task only has a log once it has started running, so one submitted moments ago comes back with 'available' false and its run state rather than an error: wait, then read it again.
get_task_log.display_str_template: Read the log for Internet Archive task {0}.
get_task_log.name: get_task_log

parameters.description: The task to read, as returned by 'List tasks', 'Submit a task', an upload or a metadata change.
parameters.name: task_id

parameters.description: How many lines from the end of the log to return (1-5000). Defaults to 200.
parameters.name: tail_lines

list_item_files.description: Page through the files inside an item. Each file comes back with the exact name archive.org knows it by, its size, format, checksums and a direct download URL. Filter to the originals to skip the thumbnails, OCR text and transcodes archive.org generates from them, or narrow by part of a name.
list_item_files.name: list_item_files

parameters.description: The item whose files to list.
parameters.name: identifier

parameters.description: Only return files of these kinds. 'Original' is what was uploaded; 'derivative' is what archive.org made from it. Choosing none returns every file.
parameters.name: sources

options.label: Derivative: generated by archive.org from an original
Metadata: generated to describe the item

parameters.description: Optional. Only return files whose name contains this text, matched without regard to case.
parameters.name: name_contains

parameters.description: How many files to return (1-1000). Defaults to 100.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: Zero-based position to start from, for paging. Pass the previous run's 'next_offset'. Defaults to 0.
parameters.name: offset

list_tasks.description: The background jobs archive.org is running on your items. Every upload, metadata change and review becomes one of these, so this is how a workflow follows what it started. 'Active' holds the queued, running, failed and paused ones; 'Finished' holds the ones that have already run.
list_tasks.name: list_tasks

parameters.description: Only return tasks for this item. Leave blank for every task on the account. '*' and '%' work as wildcards.
parameters.name: identifier

parameters.description: Which lists to read. Defaults to the active tasks; choose both to see a task whether it has finished or not.
parameters.name: task_sets

options.label: Active: queued, running, failed or paused
Finished: tasks that have already run

parameters.description: Only return tasks running this command.
parameters.name: command

options.label: Derive: regenerate the item's derivative files
Fixer: run a repair operation on the item
Make dark: hide the item from the public
Make undark: make a hidden item public again
Rename: give the item a new identifier
Back up: copy the item to a second server
Book operation: run a book-specific operation

parameters.description: Only return tasks in this state. Applies to the active list.
parameters.name: run_state

parameters.description: Only return tasks submitted by this account's email address.
parameters.name: submitter

parameters.description: Only return tasks submitted on or after this day.
parameters.name: submitted_on_or_after

parameters.description: Only return tasks submitted on or before this day.
parameters.name: submitted_on_or_before

parameters.description: How many tasks to return (1-500). Defaults to 50.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: The cursor from the previous run, to continue from where it stopped.
parameters.name: cursor

scrape_items.description: Walk a whole search result set, however large, a page at a time. Each run returns up to 10,000 items and a cursor; feed that cursor back in, with the same query, to get the next page, and stop when no cursor comes back. Turn on 'Count only' to get the size of a result set without any of it.
scrape_items.name: scrape_items

parameters.description: What to walk, in the same query language 'Search items' uses.
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: Only return items of these kinds. Choosing several matches any of them; choosing none searches everything.
parameters.name: media_types

options.label: Collection: an item that holds other items

parameters.description: Only return items in this collection, by its identifier: 'nasa', 'librivoxaudio', 'prelinger'. A collection is itself an item, so its identifier is the last part of its archive.org URL.
parameters.name: collection

parameters.description: Which metadata fields each result should carry. Defaults to the identifier, title, media type, date and download count.
parameters.name: fields

parameters.description: How to order the results. Leave blank for archive.org's own relevance ranking.
parameters.name: sort_by

parameters.description: Which direction to sort in. Defaults to descending.
parameters.name: sort_order

parameters.description: How many items to return per page (100-10,000). archive.org refuses a page smaller than 100. Defaults to 100.
parameters.name: count

parameters.description: The cursor returned by the previous run, to continue from where it stopped. Leave blank to start at the beginning.
parameters.name: cursor

parameters.description: Return how many items match and nothing else. Much faster than fetching a page when the count is all you need.
parameters.name: total_only

search_items.description: Search archive.org's 40 million items: books, films, concerts, software, images and datasets. This is the search behind the site's own search box, and it takes the same query language: bare words search everything, 'field:value' narrows to one field, quotes match a phrase, and AND, OR and NOT combine clauses. Reaches the first 10,000 results; use 'Scrape items' to walk a whole result set.
search_items.name: search_items

parameters.description: What to search for. Plain words search every field; 'creator:', 'title:', 'subject:', 'description:', 'uploader:' and 'date:' narrow to one.
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: Only return items of these kinds. Choosing several matches any of them; choosing none searches everything.
parameters.name: media_types

options.label: Collection: an item that holds other items

parameters.description: Only return items in this collection, by its identifier: 'nasa', 'librivoxaudio', 'prelinger'. A collection is itself an item, so its identifier is the last part of its archive.org URL.
parameters.name: collection

parameters.description: Which metadata fields each result should carry. Defaults to the identifier, title, media type, date and download count.
parameters.name: fields

parameters.description: How to order the results. Leave blank for archive.org's own relevance ranking.
parameters.name: sort_by

parameters.description: Which direction to sort in. Defaults to descending.
parameters.name: sort_order

parameters.description: How many items to return (1-500). Defaults to 25.
parameters.name: results_per_page

parameters.description: Which page of results to return, starting at 1. Page times results per page cannot exceed 10,000.
parameters.name: page

submit_task.description: Ask archive.org to run a job on one of your items. Deriving regenerates the thumbnails, transcodes and OCR text after its files change; darkening hides an item from the public and undarkening puts it back; renaming gives it a new identifier. The job is queued rather than run, and the task id that comes back is what 'Get a task log' reads.
submit_task.display_str_template: Submit an Internet Archive task on {0}.
submit_task.name: submit_task

parameters.description: The item to run the job on.
parameters.name: identifier

parameters.description: Which job to run. Deleting an item outright is not offered: it cannot be undone, and archive.org's own guidance is to darken the item instead.
parameters.name: command

options.label: Derive: regenerate the item's derivative files
Fixer: run a repair operation on the item
Make dark: hide the item from the public
Make undark: make a hidden item public again
Rename: give the item a new identifier
Back up: copy the item to a second server
Book operation: run a book-specific operation

parameters.description: Why the job is being run. Required for darkening and undarkening: archive.org keeps it on the item's history.
parameters.name: comment

parameters.description: The identifier to move the item to. Required when renaming, ignored otherwise.
parameters.name: new_identifier

parameters.description: Any other arguments the command takes, as names and values. Most jobs need none.
parameters.name: arguments

parameters.description: Where the job sits in archive.org's queue, from -10 to 10. Leave blank for the default.
parameters.name: priority

parameters.description: When the account already has too many jobs in flight, queue this one at a lower priority instead of refusing it. Worth turning on when a workflow submits jobs in bulk.
parameters.name: accept_reduced_priority

update_item_metadata.description: Change the metadata on an item you own: its title, description, subjects, licence or any other field, or on one of its files. Setting a field that is not there adds it; setting one that is replaces it; a field already holding the value you asked for is left alone, so running the step twice is not an error. The change is queued as a background task, and the task id comes back so a later step can watch it - or 'changed' comes back false when there was nothing to do.
update_item_metadata.name: update_item_metadata

parameters.description: The item whose metadata to change.
parameters.name: identifier

parameters.description: The fields to add or replace, as field names and values: 'title', 'description', 'subject', 'licenseurl', or a field of your own. 'collection' and 'mediatype' are not ordinary fields: changing either moves or re-types the item, which archive.org only allows privileged accounts to do.
parameters.name: fields

parameters.description: Fields to delete from the item, chosen from the ones it currently carries.
parameters.name: remove_fields

parameters.description: Leave blank to edit the item's own metadata. Choose a file to edit that file's metadata instead.
parameters.name: file_name

parameters.description: Where the change sits in archive.org's queue, from -10 to 10. Leave blank for the default.
parameters.name: priority

upload_file.description: Add a file to an item that already exists. Uploading a name the item already holds replaces that file; turn on 'Keep the previous version' to have archive.org move the old one into the item's history instead.
upload_file.display_str_template: Upload a file to the Internet Archive item {0}.
upload_file.name: upload_file

parameters.description: The item to add the file to.
parameters.name: identifier

parameters.description: The file to upload: choose a file, or point at a document produced by an earlier step.
parameters.name: file

parameters.description: The name to store the file under. Filled in from the file you choose.
parameters.name: file_name

parameters.description: Whether archive.org should regenerate the item's derivatives after this upload. On by default.
parameters.name: queue_derive

parameters.description: When this replaces an existing file, keep the old one in the item's history rather than overwriting it.
parameters.name: keep_old_version

description: Search the Internet Archive's library of 40 million free books, films, concerts, images, software and datasets, read any item's metadata and files, download a file, and upload your own: create items, add and remove files, edit metadata, follow the background tasks archive.org runs on them, see how often an item is viewed and where its readers came from, and leave a review.
